AWS implementation

Building blocks and services — AWS
Building blockService / componentImplementation responsibility
01Catalog & contextAmazon S3 ↗Version input or output objects and configure access, retention, and atomic publishing conventions.
02Candidate retrievalBedrock Knowledge Bases ↗Build ingestion and indexing; enforce document permissions before returning evidence. Managed retrieval does not automatically supply your application ACLs.
03Score candidatesSageMaker AI custom endpoint ↗Deploy a task-specific model for scoring or ranking. The endpoint is a host, not a pretrained universal ranker.
04Re-rank constraintsAWS Lambda ↗The named service hosts application code; supply validation, adapters, and business logic yourself.
05Published choicesClient / device codeRuns in the client or existing interface. No managed cloud service is required for this block.

Implementation note. Candidate retrieval can use vector search or a different index. A relevance scorer and business re-ranking policy remain separate responsibilities.
Notation and operational boundaries
  • Rounded block: client, device, or human actor.
  • Rectangle: processing or model capability. Diamond: a decision or authorization gate.
  • Cylinder: persisted data. Stacked marks: queue or stream.
  • Solid arrow: primary data or execution path. Dashed arrow: a control, repeat, or bypass path.
  • Dashed enclosure: logical scope, not a shared cloud or network boundary.

Production deployments also need identity, secrets management, network rules, observability, budgets, deadlines, and failure handling. Follow the linked service documentation and confirm region and model support.

Design analysis

WHEN TO USE

The product needs ranked recommendations or search results.

EXAMPLE

A reading app orders relevant articles without exposing chat.

TRADEOFF

Fast candidate retrieval may eliminate good items before ranking begins.

FAILURE & RECOVERY

Feedback loops or cold starts: evaluate coverage and define exploration policies.

EVALUATION

Measure retrieval recall, ranking quality, diversity, and fresh-item coverage.

Production checkpoints
  • Define input contracts and measurable success criteria.
  • Check permissions and validate model outputs outside the model.
  • Set budgets, deadlines, cancellation, retry limits, and recovery behavior.
  • Version models, instructions, and data; evaluate before release and retain a rollback path.
  • Minimize sensitive content in traces and define retention policies.
